steps.body: Solving a two-step inequality uses the same undo-moves as an equation — with a POSITIVE coefficient, the direction never changes. 3x + 2 > 14: subtract 2, divide by 3: x > 4.

widget.prompt: Solve 3x + 2 > 14. The beam is tilted because the sentence is TRUE — keep it that way while you clear and split.
widget.successFeedback: x > 4. Two units came off both pans, then both sides split into 3 — and the beam never changed which way it leaned, so the > never had to move.
widget.unbalancedFeedback: The tilt reversed, which means the sentence stopped being true. Something happened to one pan only. Undo and pair every move.
widget.notIsolatedFeedback: The sentence is still true — every move so far was legal. But x is not alone yet: clear the units from both pans, then split into equal groups.
widget.missFeedback: Keep the x-tiles on the pan — they are what you are solving for. Clear the units from both sides, then split.
widget.notFlippedFeedback: The comparator and the beam are pointing opposite ways. Nothing here needed a flip — adding, subtracting and splitting into groups all leave the tilt alone.

predict.prompt: Solving an inequality — are the steps the SAME as an equation's?

options.label: Same — until a negative multiplies or divides

predict.reveal: Add, subtract, and positive scaling all work unchanged — the one landmine is multiplying or dividing by a negative. Everything else is equation muscle memory.

steps.body: Watch the set while you divide — this time the number is positive.

widget.prompt: 3x > 12 is where the last step left you, and the line already shows which numbers make it true. Get x standing on its own — and when you are done, the line must still show those same numbers.
widget.successFeedback: x > 4, and the line finished exactly where it started. Dividing by a POSITIVE 3 keeps every number where it was — the direction only ever changes when the number you divide by is negative. Hold on to this picture: it is the half of the rule the next lesson breaks.
widget.fallbackFeedback: Test a number on each side of the endpoint in the original 3x > 12 and see which side really works.

predict.prompt: You are about to divide both sides of 3x > 12 by 3. What happens to the number line?

options.label: Nothing moves — the set is already right, only the writing changes
The ray swings to the other side of 4
The endpoint slides toward 0 because both sides got smaller

predict.reveal: Nothing moves. 3x > 12 and x > 4 are two ways of writing the SAME set, and dividing both sides by a positive number cannot change which numbers work. The ray only ever swings when the divider is negative — that is the whole difference, and it is the next lesson's story.

commonBuilds.feedback: Dividing by a POSITIVE 4 never flips the direction: x<4, not x>4.
That's only the first step (4x<16). Finish by dividing by 4: x<4.

widget.missFeedback: Undo the constant first, then divide — the inequality sign stays put when dividing by a positive.
widget.successFeedback: Yes — add 1 (4x<16), divide by 4 (positive, no flip): x<4.
